summary: High-level security and privacy review focused on data handling: prompt retention, PII/PHI considerations, encryption and KMS, SSO/RBAC, and confirmation that Redwood does not train models on customer data. Agreement to share certs and schedule deeper infra session.
topics: Data residency and VPC/private deployment options
Encryption at rest/in transit and KMS/HSM integration
'No training on customer data' commitment and exceptions
transcript:
[00:00] Alice (AE - Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're on the 14:23, I see Priya, Marcus, Evan and Nina, thanks. Quick agenda: certs, data flow, retention, KMS, SSO and the training question.
[00:15] Dr. Priya Rao (CISO - Alpine): Yep, thanks. We wanted to focus on three things: how long prompts are stored, whether PHI could be ingested and used to improve models, and how we can get audit logs for compliance.
[00:30] Sam (SE - Redwood): Great, yep. On certs we are SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 certified, I'll drop the pack after. Our hosted API by default keeps logs for X days- sorry X is a placeholder, we keep request traces for 30 days for observability unless customer config says otherwise.
[00:45] Marcus (Head of AI): Can you clarify 'keeps logs' — is that raw prompt text or metadata? We need to know if any customer prompt content is used for training.
[01:00] Sam (SE - Redwood): Right. Short answer: we do not train our public or internal models on customer data. We have a strict policy — um, let me phrase — we don't feed customer prompt content back into model training pipelines. There's an internal audit trail that shows ingestion pipelines are gated.
[01:15] Evan (Legal): Is that contractual? We need 'no training' as a contractual commitment in the DPA.
[01:30] Alice: We can add the language. We also offer Private deployment — for Alpine's use-case we can do a VPC-private control plane or on-prem variant so data never leaves your environment.
[01:45] Nina (Infra): For VPC/private, how do you handle KMS? We use AWS KMS and want HSM backed keys for some scopes.
[02:00] Sam: We integrate with customer-managed KMS — AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault; we also support HSM-backed keys via partner integrations. For private deploys keys can stay in your account and Redwood services never see unencrypted material.
[02:15] Dr. Priya: And encryption at rest — are tokens or embeddings stored encrypted?
[02:30] Sam: Yes, at rest everything is encrypted with customer-specific keys where configured. For hosted we use our managed keys by default but customers can bring their own.
[02:45] Marcus: About prompt retention — if we have clinical notes that hit the prompt, what's retention and purge flow?
[03:00] Sam: By default request logs are kept for 30 days for troubleshooting. We offer configurable retention windows down to zero days for sensitive workloads in Dedicated/Private. We also have an API to purge customer data on request; it cascades through caches and KV stores but note rollback windows, so we need to schedule account-level purge.
[03:30] Dr. Priya: Do you do any keyword redaction or PII detection transitively?
[03:45] Sam: We have optional PII scrubbing tooling as a pre-processor that customers can enable; it's not on by default. For PHI/healthcare workloads we recommend running that or using Private deployment.
[04:00] Evan: HIPAA — if we sign BAAs, what's Redwood's role? Are you a business associate?
[04:15] Alice: We can sign a BAA for Private deployments; for hosted we need legal to confirm scope. We'll coordinate on specifics.
[04:30] Nina: Audit logs — we need per-request traceability, user identity, IPs and redaction markers. Can we get streaming logs to our SIEM?
[04:45] Sam: Yes — we provide audit logs that include request IDs, routing decisions, model version, tokens in metadata form; full plaintext is optional and can be included only if you opt-in. We can stream logs to S3 or to a SIEM via secure forwarder.
[05:00] Marcus: One more on model variants — you mentioned fallback to smaller models; do those variants ever have different training regimes? Any chance customer data from one tenant could influence another?
[05:15] Sam: No cross-tenant training. Models that are 'served' are either open weights we host or Redwood-managed finetuned variants but none of our hosted / customer inputs are used to finetune. We have a separation boundary and retention controls.
[05:30] Dr. Priya: Can you point to the audit that proves that? A high-level architecture doc would help.
[05:45] Alice: We'll share the data-flow diagram and the internal audit report excerpts.
[06:00] Evan: For DPA we also need clarity on subprocessors and where data may transit — US only or global?
[06:15] Sam: We operate regions in US and EU. By default traffic is routed regionally; you can pin to EU-only with Private or Dedicated.
[06:30] Marcus: Is there a way to run inference on our on-prem hardware?
[06:45] Sam: Yes, Redwood Private supports on-prem deployments; the control plane can be customer-managed and can be air-gapped if needed.
[07:00] Dr. Priya: Back to training — can you confirm the exact wording you recommend in the DPA? We need something like 'Redwood shall not use Customer Content to train any models, whether internal or external'.
[07:15] Alice: That's consistent with our standard clause. We'll draft it.
[07:30] Nina: Keys — if we rotate keys in our KMS, what's the process for decrypting stored embeddings or cached KV?
[07:45] Sam: We support key rotation; when you rotate keys we rewrap the data envelope keys — there's a short rewrap window but no plaintext exposure; for large caches we coordinate a maintenance window.
[08:00] Marcus: How about RBAC and SSO — we use SAML SSO via Okta. Can we enforce role-level restrictions so only certain users can call models or see transcript logs?
[08:15] Jordan (CSM - Redwood): Yes, our Console supports SSO via SAML/SCIM integration with Okta and provides RBAC roles; we can map groups to roles and restrict log access.
[08:30] Dr. Priya: Will those RBAC events appear in audit logs?
[08:45] Sam: Yes, admin actions, role changes, API key generation are all logged with user context.
[09:00] Marcus: Any caveats about streaming responses and logs? For streaming tokens, do you persist in-flight token traces?
[09:15] Sam: Streams are chunked; we don't persist raw streaming token traces beyond request logs unless you enable extended logging.
[09:30] Evan: Regarding encryption compliance, do you have attestation for HSM use?
[09:45] Sam: For HSM backed KMS we rely on the cloud provider's HSM attestation; for on-prem we can integrate with customer HSMs and provide integration notes.
[10:00] Dr. Priya: Data residency — if we route EU traffic, can you guarantee that backups won't be replicated to US?
[10:15] Sam: For Dedicated/Private we can guarantee EU-only processing and backups; for hosted we have region pinning but we need contract language to ensure no cross-region backups.
[10:30] Marcus: Scoring risk — if a model inadvertently outputs PHI, what's the remediation flow?
[10:45] Alice: Incident response: you open a ticket, we provide forensics and data purge if needed; we have an incident runbook and can escalate to executive security contacts.
[11:00] Nina: Do you keep a copy of user uploaded files when we use file-based inputs?
[11:15] Sam: File inputs are handled similarly to text prompts; retention policy applies, and you can opt to disable retention.
[11:30] Dr. Priya: Can you do an attested penetration test for us?
[11:45] Alice: We run third-party pen tests regularly and can share the summary report under NDA.
[12:00] Marcus: A small nit: earlier you said 'we don't train on customer data' — is telemetry like usage metrics ever used for product telemetry that could indirectly influence model behavior?
[12:15] Sam: We use anonymized telemetry for platform performance and product improvements — not for model training. We'll annotate what telemetry buckets exist.
[12:30] Evan: For contract, we'll want clear definitions of Customer Content and Derived Data, e.g., embeddings derived from prompts; who owns them?
[12:45] Alice: Customer owns Customer Content; Derived Data definitions we'll align on in DPA. Typically customers own embeddings generated from their content, but we also need rights to operate the service. We'll propose language.
[13:00] Marcus: Can you describe redaction tools again — inline scrubbing vs pre/post processing?
[13:15] Sam: We offer SDK hooks for pre-processing to scrub PII before send, and post-processing for redaction in logs. Both approaches are supported.
[13:30] Dr. Priya: For HIPAA workloads, do you recommend Private deployment only?
[13:45] Sam: Yes, Private or Dedicated with BAA and VPC isolation is our recommendation for production PHI.
[14:00] Evan: One more on legal retention: if a subpoena requests user prompts, who do we call?
[14:15] Alice: Standard legal process, Redwood will follow the DPA and subpoena handling process; we'll coordinate with your legal team.
[14:30] Marcus: Ok, recapping next steps: Alice to send certs and DPA language, Sam to run infra deep dive, Evan to return DPA redlines.
[14:45] Alice: Correct — thanks all. We'll email the artifacts and propose times for the infra call.
[15:00] Dr. Priya: Thanks, that's helpful.
[15:05] (call ends)

Notes: occasional transcription glitches: 'HSM' heard as 'HSMM' briefly, 'KV cache' sometimes 'K-V cache' in raw transcript.
notes: Transcript contains realistic speech patterns, some mishearings of acronyms and short crosstalk. Customer focused heavily on PHI, retention, and contractual 'no training' commitments.
